commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: add the B200 NVFP4 TP2 agentic preset
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a `b200_tp2_kv_offload` tuned preset to `recipes/models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.yaml`: NVIDIA's tuned configuration for serving `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4` on two B200s for long-context agentic coding traffic. The baseline command and every other rendering are unchanged; the preset appears in the command builder's Preset row for B200 with the `nvfp4` variant.

## Claims

- TP2 with expert parallelism on two B200s, MTP with three draft tokens (the recipe's existing `spec_decoding: mtp` mode), FP8 KV cache, `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16`, `--async-scheduling`, `--block-size 64`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, `--max-num-seqs 48`, `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, and vLLM native CPU KV offload with `--kv-offloading-size 160` GiB summed over the two ranks.
- Turns the default-on `encoder_parallel` feature off and selects the Python frontend, matching the measured configuration.
- Measured on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0`, two B200 SXM 180 GB, a 942-request multi-turn agentic coding trace (about 64k mean input tokens, outputs capped at 12k) at concurrency 16 with real MTP acceptance: 936 output tok/s/GPU, 8.7 ms mean ITL, 0.70 s mean TTFT, all requests completed. The table is in the preset's runbook.
- Bumps `meta.date_updated`.

## Validation

- The exact rendered flag set was served on the pinned image on two B200s on an NVIDIA cluster against the trace above; the startup log shows every flag taken as given (MTP, native offload connector, FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend, 37 GiB of GPU KV per rank). No public run link yet; an InferenceX AgentX lane with the same settings is being prepared, and this preset's `source` will be repointed to it when it lands.
- The `Recipes / Validate` check passes and the preview deployment renders the preset: the B200 NVFP4 Preset row composes `vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm` plus the preset's flags, the parsers and the MTP speculative config, with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` dropped; the baseline B200 command and every other rendering are unchanged. The vLLM `/pr-checklist` skill was not run.

## Details

- A preset rather than a change to `hardware_overrides.blackwell`: these settings are workload-specific (admission cap, offload tier), so they should not alter the baseline B200 command.
- The runbook states that further concurrencies and the same-image comparison against the recipe's baseline command are being collected; they will follow in a separate PR.
- `source` points at this PR.

## Overview

Update the GB300 AgentX presets of MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (`gb300_agentx_agg`, `gb300_agentx_pd`) to the Dynamo + vLLM lanes of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4631](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4631) (head `5d3aa21b`). Only touches `recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml`.

- **Frontend:** `DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens` (Dynamo's fastokens tokenizer backend). Frontend tokenization of 100K+ token prompts drops from about 150 ms to about 1 ms per request, which comes straight off TTFT.
- **Mooncake pool:** 160 GB to 180 GB per rank. Run etcd, NATS, the Mooncake master and the frontend on a host without engine workers, so the trays' host DRAM goes to the pool.
- **Measured points:** 6 DEP2 prefill + DEP8 now runs up to 400 sessions, and DEP16 up to 360. The table, tuning rules and source revision are updated.

## Validation

- Measured in the lane's sweep ([run 41103476412](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/41103476412)): 6 prefill + DEP8 at 280/320/360/400 sessions: 93.1k/100.5k/107.9k/114.5k tok/s/GPU at 240/229/224/219 tok/s/user, TTFT p90 2.7-5.9 s; 6 prefill + DEP16 at 300/360: 75.0k/85.8k at 296/285, TTFT p90 1.8/2.4 s.

commits.pr_title: [Docs][ROCm] Mistral Large 4 recipe: adds TP4 and lowest-latency presets
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Adds TP4 and lowest-latency (specialized decode) presets to the Mistral Large 4 recipe, so MI350X and MI355X both offer them for the FP8 and Quark MXFP4 checkpoints. Also fixes the AMD `docker run` command.

New presets:
- MI350X, MXFP4 (Quark): `mi350x_mxfp4_tp4`, `mi350x_mxfp4_tp4_specialized`
- MI355X, FP8: `mi355x_tp4`, `mi355x_tp4_specialized`
- MI355X, MXFP4 (Quark): `mi355x_mxfp4_tp4`, `mi355x_mxfp4_tp4_specialized`

TP4 is the baseline at `--tensor-parallel-size 4` with DSpark. Lowest latency adds `--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'`. FP8 also sets `VLLM_FP8_MOE_REQUANT_ACT=a4w4`. Quark sets no requant variables, because its routed experts are already MXFP4 a4w4. The MI355X specialized presets keep the baseline's `--max-num-seqs 128`. The MI350X Quark one sets `--max-num-seqs 64` to match the existing MI350X FP8 preset.

**AMD `docker run` fix.** `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:mistral-large-4` has no entrypoint. Setting `docker_serve_command: "vllm serve"` for mi350x and mi355x renders `<image> vllm serve <model> …`.

## Test Result

All checks passed.
| MI355X preset | c1 TPOT p50 | c4 TPOT p50 | AL (c1 / c4) | KV cache per replica |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP8 TP4 (a8w4) | 3.75 ms | 6.26 ms | 2.91 / 3.03 | 2.18M tokens |
| FP8 specialized decode (a4w4) | 3.56 ms | 6.14 ms | 2.85 / 2.99 | 2.09M tokens |
| Quark TP4 | 3.85 ms | 6.05 ms | 2.88 / 3.03 | 2.19M tokens |
| Quark specialized decode | 3.60 ms | 6.03 ms | 2.86 / 3.03 | 2.09M tokens |

- Specialized decode vs TP4 + DSpark: 1.05x (FP8) and 1.07x (Quark) at c1, about 1.0x at c4. One DSpark verify step at 8k input (c1) takes 12.4 ms vs 13.6 ms (FP8) and 12.4 ms vs 13.0 ms (Quark).
- `--max-num-seqs`: every setting started and served with `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE` applied on all ranks, and none hit the "cannot be IPC-exported" abort. The custom all-reduce pool was allocated with expandable segments off. 64 and 128 gave the same TPOT (c1 3.64 vs 3.60 ms).
- `--monokernel` selects the same specialized decode as `--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'` (identical log lines). The Quark model card's command passed.

commits.pr_title: [Docs][ROCm] Add MiniMax-M3.1-Flash MI355X TP4 AgentX preset
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add the opt-in `mi355x_agentx` preset to the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash recipe: the MI355X TP4 AgentX lane from [InferenceX #4671](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4671) on the Quark MXFP4 checkpoint, concurrency 1 to 64.

## Claims

- Adds one preset, scoped to the `mxfp4` variant, with seven concurrency points that the builder can render: 1/2/4/8 (seven-token DSpark with mono decode, FP8 KV cache), 16/32 (seven-token DSpark with DBO, NVFP4 KV cache, 0.85 memory), and 64 (three-token DSpark with DBO and a host-DRAM KV tier through `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, 0.90 memory).
- Every point's generated command carries the same serving flags as the InferenceX run for that point.
- The runbook records measured results and two limitations (below).
- No existing rendering changes.

## Validation

From a `vllm-project/recipes` checkout at `d460fcc`, with this branch as the `vllm` source:

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir "$VLLM_CHECKOUT/recipes"
node --test scripts/test-guide-html.mjs scripts/test-presets.mjs scripts/test-schema.mjs
pre-commit run typos --files recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml
```

The source validator passes, 47 of 47 renderer tests pass, and `typos` passes. Building the JSON API on `main` and on this branch gives 22,575 identical files; the only differences are the new `presets/mi355x_agentx.json` and the new entry in the two parent JSONs (`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.json` and the promoted `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4.json`).

All seven rendered commands were compared flag by flag with the `vllm serve` commands in the InferenceX job logs. Serving flags and relevant environment variables match at every point, except that the harness flags (`--host`, `--port`, `--device-ids`, `--served-model-name`, `--disable-uvicorn-access-log`, `--max-model-len`, `--trust-remote-code`) are not part of the preset, throughput runs used synthetic rejection where the preset keeps block rejection, and `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_SP_PREFILL=1` (set at concurrency 64 by InferenceX) is omitted because it had no effect on this checkpoint.

Existing GPU evidence, not a new GPU run from this PR: [InferenceX run 41003224750](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/41003224750) at `a328b4435` passed all seven performance points and GSM8K at concurrency 8, 32 and 64 (0.964, 0.959, 0.957 strict exact match, 1,319 samples each). Per-point interactivity and throughput are in the runbook (single run).

## Details

**Not a duplicate.** The recipe has presets for B300, GB200 and GB300 but none for MI355X AgentX. Open PRs touching this model are code changes (#64448, #64273), not recipe presets.

**Why the DBO points pass the DBO flags directly.** The `prefill_dbo_sp` feature's modes set their own thresholds (8192, or 16384 with SP on the default checkpoint only) and a feature's flags win over a preset's `args`. This lane runs the 16384-token DBO threshold without SP, so the preset passes `--enable-dbo` and the thresholds itself, with the V2 model runner env the feature would set.

**Limitations, also in the runbook.**
- Concurrency 64 needed a rerun: the first attempt hung at its first load from the host KV tier (23 fetches in progress, none completing, then a `sample_tokens` RPC timeout) and the rerun passed. The offload point is less proven than the others.
- Sequence-parallel prefill does not apply to the Quark checkpoint: the server logged it as off even with the variable set.

AI assistance was used (Claude Sonnet 5.5, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, via Claude Code): it drafted the preset, ran the validation above, and compared the rendered commands with the InferenceX job logs. The submitter reviewed the changes.

commits.pr_title: [Docs][ROCm] Add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MI355X TP8 concurrency-1 AgentX preset
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add the opt-in `mi355x_agentx_tp8` preset to the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe: the TP8, concurrency-1 AgentX point from [InferenceX #4666](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4666), served with `--monokernel` on a nightly that carries [#64101](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64101) (mono decode at TP8 on MI355X).

## Claims

- Adds one preset with one point (concurrency 1, TP8) for MI355X, pinned to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1@sha256:3c634cc2…7291`.
- The generated command carries the same serving flags as the InferenceX run; the TP8 point keeps `--monokernel` and GPU-resident Engram tables (`cpu_offload: false`), with one sequence at a time and 32768-token prefill chunks, as the TP4 concurrency-1 point does.
- The runbook documents that TP8 mono is a concurrency-1 configuration and needs a build with #64101.
- No existing rendering changes.

## Validation

From a `vllm-project/recipes` checkout at `d460fcc`, with this branch as the `vllm` source:

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir "$VLLM_CHECKOUT/recipes"
node --test scripts/test-guide-html.mjs scripts/test-presets.mjs scripts/test-schema.mjs
```

The source validator passes and 47 of 47 renderer tests pass. Building the JSON API on `main` and on this branch gives 22,575 identical files; the only differences are the new `presets/mi355x_agentx_tp8.json` and the new entry in the two parent recipe JSONs (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.json`, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017.json`).

The rendered TP8 command was compared flag by flag with the `vllm serve` command in the InferenceX job log. Every serving flag matches; the only differences are harness flags (`--host`, `--port`, `--device-ids`, `--served-model-name`, `--disable-uvicorn-access-log`) and `--max-model-len 1048576`, which equals the recipe's `context_length`.

Existing GPU evidence, not a new GPU run from this PR:

| Evidence | Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [InferenceX run 41098938196](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/41098938196), `fa9d48627` | MI355X TP8 concurrency-1 performance point, nightly-335dd77b | Passed: 362 of 373 requests, interactivity p50 696.9 / p90 685.5 tokens/s/user, TTFT p50 0.17 s (single run) |
| Same run, GSM8K | TP8 concurrency 1, real block rejection | 0.972 strict exact match, 1,319 samples |

`pre-commit run typos` flags `UE8M0` at line 1306 of this file. That line is not in this diff and the same failure occurs on `main`.

## Details

**Not a duplicate.** I found no open or merged PR that adds a TP8 preset for this recipe; #63665, #63344 and #63560 cover the TP2/TP4 `mi355x_agentx` preset, and #64589 adds an unrelated MI325X preset. This preset is separate from `mi355x_agentx` because `source` (InferenceX key and revision) is per preset, and this lane has its own key, revision and image pin.

**Limits.** #64101 validated TP8 mono with six DSpark drafts; this lane runs five (the recipe's value), measured by the InferenceX run above. The preset makes no claim beyond concurrency 1. The `mi355x_agentx` preset is untouched.

The preset is placed at the end of the presets block, away from the MI325X preset proposed in #64589, to avoid a textual conflict between the two.

AI assistance was used (Claude Sonnet 5.5, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, via Claude Code): it drafted the preset, ran the validation above and compared the rendered command with the InferenceX job log. The submitter reviewed the changes.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Preserve whitespace in HYV4 argument names
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Preserve schema property names exactly in HYV4 streaming tool calls. For an integer property named `" count "`, streaming currently emits `{"count": "7"}` while non-streaming returns `{" count ": 7}`.

This addresses the argument-key whitespace case explicitly excluded from #60788.

## Claims

- Preserve whitespace in argument names in both completed-pair and partial-value streaming paths.
- Use the exact key for schema type lookup and keep `"count"` and `" count "` distinct, matching non-streaming parsing.

## Validation

Local results rerun on 2026-10-14 after updating to main `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`, on macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.14 and xgrammar 0.2.8. The tested patch is `04aa841822468b4bcf66c90221cbd2e5df0e1ccc`. Tests use a tokenizer stub with the real vLLM parser, protocol objects, and xgrammar; no model weights are needed.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whitespace regression suite | 156 failed, 4 passed | 160 passed |
| Both complete test files | 156 failed, 272 passed | 428 passed |

All 156 baseline failures in the complete files are the new whitespace cases; every other test passes on both sides (complete-file baseline rerun on 2026-10-30 at the same commits).

Targeted reproduction (run the same tests with the original and patched production file):

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/tool_parsers -k whitespace -q --tb=short
```

Full-file regression:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/tool_parsers/hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. The existing CPU Tool Parsers CI job runs this test directory; upstream CI has not been run for this change.

### End-to-end validation with real HYV4 weights (H20, 2026-10-30)

I served the real `Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview-FP8` checkpoint and compared streaming against non-streaming tool calls, before and after this PR.

**Setup**
- 1× NVIDIA H20 (SM90), vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev507+g85e199e60` wheel, torch 2.14.0+cu130.
- Only `vllm/tool_parsers/hy_v4_tool_parser.py` differs between the two runs:
  - baseline = `d5e62627a3` (sha256 `d0aa7524…`, identical to the file shipped in the wheel);
  - patched = `04aa841` (sha256 `5b38e435…`).
- Serve flags:
  ```
  vllm serve Hy4-preview-FP8 --tool-call-parser hy_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 --hf-overrides '{"num_nextn_predict_layers":0}' \
    --cpu-offload-gb 690 --cpu-offload-params experts \
    --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 1 --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92
  ```
  The routed experts (MxFP8, HUMMING backend) sit in host memory, since the model does not fit on one GPU.
- Request:
  - one tool `record` whose only property is `" count "` (integer, one leading and one trailing space);
  - prompt asks the model to call it with 7;
  - `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, `reasoning_effort=no_think`.
  - The same body is sent once with `stream=false` and once with `stream=true`. The streamed arguments are rebuilt from the raw SSE deltas.
- There is no grammar or logit bias beyond what vLLM applies for each `tool_choice`.

**Results**

| tool_choice | non-stream (both) | baseline stream | patched stream |
|---|---|---|---|
| `required` | `{" count ": 7}` | `{"count": "7"}` ❌ | `{" count ": 7}` ✅ |
| named `record` | `{" count ": 7}` | `{"count": "7"}` ❌ | `{" count ": 7}` ✅ |

- In each case, the generated token ids are identical across all four requests (baseline/patched × stream/non-stream), so the difference comes from the parser alone.
- The model emits the atomic `:opensource` marker tokens (ids 120033–120043), so this exercises the token-id streaming path.
- On baseline, the stripped key no longer matches the schema, so the value also loses its integer type (`"7"`).

A tiny-random HYV4 model run on the same host showed the same pattern:
- guided (string) path: baseline stream `{"count": "-451"}`, patched `{" count ": -451}`;
- token-id path: same as above;
- non-stream `{" count ": -451}` throughout.

**Unrelated observation**
- With `tool_choice="auto"`, the real model produced a malformed call: `<arg_key:opensource> count </arg_value:opensource><arg_value:opensource>7…`, i.e. the key is closed with `</arg_value>`.
- Non-streaming then returns no tool call and puts the text in `content`, while streaming emits `record` with `{}`.
- Baseline and patched behave identically here, so it is outside this PR's scope. It is a separate stream/non-stream divergence on malformed output.

## Details

`_extract_streaming_incremental` strips keys in two places before schema lookup and argument tracking. This changes valid property names, can stringify non-string values, and can collapse two distinct properties. Remove those two normalizations; the structural-tag grammar already preserves exact schema keys.

Regression coverage includes whitespace-only names, seven value types, colliding trimmed names in both orders, whole/token/character chunks, both token suffix variants, emitted JSON prefixes, and state cleanup between tool calls. Four grammar cases check exact required/optional keys.

Upstream overlap was rechecked on 2026-10-14 at main `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`: both key normalizations remain. No direct duplicate was found. #60788 excludes this case; #59620 handles truncated calls and inter-tag whitespace; #61205 limits grammar whitespace length. Those changes do not preserve whitespace inside argument keys.

AI assistance was used for implementation, test preparation, review, and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honor draft moe/attention backend overrides for MRV2 standalone draft model
commits.pr_body:
Proposed title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honor draft moe/attention backend overrides for MRV2 standalone draft model

## Purpose

With model runner V2, `method: draft_model` (`StandaloneARSpeculator`) silently ignores `moe_backend` and `attention_backend` from `--speculative-config`. The draft inherits the target's `--moe-backend` / `--attention-backend` instead.

- V1 honors all three draft overrides (`moe_backend`, `attention_backend`, `kv_cache_dtype`) through `_create_draft_vllm_config` in `llm_base_proposer.py`, which `draft_model.py` inherits (#37880, #39930).
- The V2 standalone drafter (#43091) never got them. #61240 added `kv_cache_dtype` by hand. #57312 moved the V2 EAGLE/MTP overrides into `SpeculativeConfig.apply_draft_overrides` but did not touch the standalone path.

The fix builds the draft `VllmConfig` from `spec.apply_draft_overrides(self.vllm_config)`, the same way `load_eagle_model` does, and removes the hand-written `kv_cache_dtype` branch. Any new entry in `_DRAFT_VLLM_CONFIG_OVERRIDES` now reaches this drafter too.

`attn_vllm_config` is unchanged. `init_attn_backend` takes each group's backend from the constructed layer (`attn_layers[name].get_attn_backend()`), and the draft layers are built under the overridden config, so their builders already match the draft backend. No metadata builder reads `attention_config.backend` or `kernel_config.moe_backend`. The `kv_cache_dtype` condition is still needed because builders read `cache_config.cache_dtype`.

## Test Plan

- Extended `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_standalone_draft_kv_dtype_override`. It now also parametrizes the draft `moe_backend` / `attention_backend`, and asserts that the draft config gets them when set, keeps the target's when unset, and leaves the target config untouched.
- Ran this test plus `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_moe_backend_override.py` and `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_attention_backend_override.py`.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Compute prompt block hashes in the Rust frontend
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let the Rust frontend compute a request's prompt block hashes, so the engine's input thread no longer hashes long prompts while holding the GIL the engine loop needs. Revives the idea of #15652 for the Rust frontend; complementary to #63454 (cheaper engine-side hashing) and related to #43483 (frontend hashes for DP routing). Part of the long-context P/D CPU-overhead work in #63439.

## Claims

- The engine accepts frontend-computed prompt block hashes; prefix-cache hashes are unchanged (byte-identical), so cache hits, KV connectors and KV events are unaffected.
- The Rust frontend covers `sha256` and `sha256_cbor` for plain, LoRA, cache-salt and lookahead (EAGLE) requests; other requests are hashed by the engine as before.
- Removes the GIL-held prompt hashing from the engine's input thread (~50 ms per 227K-token prompt with `sha256`, ~150 ms with `sha256_cbor`), which otherwise stalls the engine loop: +9.6% decode throughput with `sha256` and +39% with `sha256_cbor` on a workload that admits long cached prompts during decode (below).

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 114 passed. `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-llm`: all passed, including known-answer vectors generated from the engine's own `Request` / `get_request_block_hasher`.
- E2E on GB300 with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, using a test-only engine patch that recomputes the hashes of every request that arrives with frontend hashes and compares them:

| Config | Requests | Hash check | Cached tokens on repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, `sha256`, LoRA | 12 (plain, salts incl. non-ASCII / 300-byte, short, LoRA, LoRA + salt) | 12/12 match | 5424/5427; a new salt or LoRA starts at 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B, `sha256_cbor`, LoRA | 12 | 12/12 match | same |
| Qwen3-1.7B + EAGLE3 (lookahead 1) | 8 | 8/8 match | same |

Benchmark (GB300, `Qwen3-0.6B`, Rust frontend, CUDA graphs): 64 streaming decode requests while fully prefix-cached 30K-token prompts (token ids, `max_tokens=1`) arrive at 20/s for 40 s. This resembles a P/D decode instance admitting long prompts. Same binaries in both arms; the "engine" arm stops the engine from advertising `prefix_hash_config`. Mean of 2 interleaved rounds (each within 2%):

| Hash | Prompt hashing in | Decode tok/s | ITL mean / p90 / p99 (ms) | Long-request TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sha256` | engine (main) | 16,870 | 3.77 / 8.36 / 10.10 | 27.6 / 46.1 |
| `sha256` | frontend (this PR) | 18,494 (+9.6%) | 3.44 / 6.51 / 9.83 | 25.6 / 37.8 |
| `sha256_cbor` | engine (main) | 13,244 | 4.80 / 10.41 / 15.64 | 34.9 / 61.1 |
| `sha256_cbor` | frontend (this PR) | 18,366 (+39%) | 3.46 / 6.45 / 10.04 | 25.6 / 35.5 |

The gain depends on how much of the engine loop the hashing displaces: a small model and a high arrival rate of long prompts make it large; larger models see a smaller relative gain.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server (both arms): `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-num-seqs 256 --prefix-caching-hash-algo {sha256,sha256_cbor} --enable-prompt-tokens-details`. For the engine arm, set `self.prefix_hash_config = None` in `EngineCore.__init__`. Client: 64 concurrent streaming `/v1/completions` (32-token prompt, `max_tokens=2000`, `ignore_eos`), measuring inter-chunk gaps; after warming 8 distinct 30K-token-id prompts into the prefix cache, send them round-robin at 20 req/s with `max_tokens=1` for 40 s.
</details>

## Details

- `EngineCoreReadyResponse.prefix_hash_config` (algorithm, `hash_block_size`, `NONE_HASH`, lookahead) is set when the engine hashes blocks. Sending `NONE_HASH` means frontends needn't reproduce the seed logic.
- `EngineCoreRequest.block_hashes` seeds `Request.block_hashes`; the existing hasher continues from there. The engine only checks the count (`(prompt_len - lookahead) // hash_block_size`) and otherwise hashes the prompt itself.
- The Rust encoder writes pickle protocol 5 / canonical CBOR exactly. It leaves to the engine: multimodal and prompt-embeds requests, `xxhash*`, keys over one 64 KiB pickle frame, and the rare requests whose strings pickle could memoize by identity.
- The Python frontend doesn't send hashes yet.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Single-launch fused scoring+top-k kernel for sparse-indexer prefill, without materializing logits
commits.pr_body: (this PR description was manually written by me) ## Summary * Adds one persistent CUDA kernel that scores every visible key of a sparse-indexer prefill chunk and selects each row's top-k keys (k = 512, 1024 or 2048) **without materializing the `[rows, keys]` logits matrix**. * One launch covers a prefill chunk of up to 16,384 query rows and up to 1M keys, including multi-request chunks. The dense path needs up to 127 call pairs (`fp8_mqa_logits` + `top_k_per_row_prefill`) for the same chunk. * The output matches the dense path up to ties at the top-k boundary: the gated path ranks 24-bit score codes, and rows the gate cannot serve are rescanned exactly in fp32. ## Motivation: what materializing the scores costs The dense prefill path writes the fp32 scores of every (query row, visible key) pair to HBM, then reads them back to select the top-k. One 16,384-row prefill chunk needs `16,384 × keys × 4 B` of logits: | Keys | Logits for one 16K-row chunk | Dense calls under the 512 MiB budget | Logits HBM traffic (write + read) | |---|---|---|---| | 16K | 1 GiB | 2 | 2 GiB | | 128K | 8 GiB | 16 | 16 GiB | | 512K | 32 GiB | 64 | 64 GiB | | 1M | 64 GiB | 127 | 128 GiB | This produces the following pattern: It gets worse with context, e.g. at ISL 512K: Two consequences: 1. **The logits budget trades KV-cache capacity against indexer speed.** During memory profiling, `sparse_attn_indexer` allocates a dummy `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` buffer, so the logits budget is part of the peak memory the KV cache is sized from. On GLM-5.x with an FP8 KV cache, one token costs 47.7 KB per GPU (78 MLA layers × 576 B + 21 indexer layers × 132 B; MLA KV is replicated across TP ranks). Measured at startup (TP4, B300, `--max-model-len 1048576`): | Configuration | Available KV memory | KV cache tokens | |---|---|---| | Dense, 512 MiB budget (default) | 115.66 GiB | 2,603,456 | | Dense, 8 GiB budget | 109.23 GiB | 2,458,816 (−5.6%) | | Fused (this PR) | 115.37 GiB | 2,596,928 (−0.25%) | At the default budget the logits buffer fits under the profiling run's other peak allocations, so it costs no KV cache. The cost is speed: rows per dense call shrink as keys grow (2²⁷ / keys), so a 128K-token prefill in 16K-token steps needs 76 dense call pairs and a 1M-token prefill needs 4,217. With the fused path (top-2048), the first four steps, whose rows see fewer than 64K keys, stay dense (21 call pairs) and every later step is one fused call: 4 at 128K, 60 at 1M. Buying fewer dense calls means raising the budget, and that memory comes straight out of the KV cache: an 8 GiB budget (one dense call per 16K-row chunk at 128K keys) costs 144,640 tokens of KV cache. One dense call per chunk at 1M keys would need 64 GiB, more than the KV cache of the entire 1M-token sequence (46.6 GiB). The fused kernel serves long-context chunks in one call each with a fixed 296 MiB workspace. 2. **The logits round trip is pure overhead.** Only k of the `keys` scores per row are needed. The fused kernel writes only a gated candidate set, about 1K–4.5K candidates per row depending on k (median on the captures below) at 6 B each, i.e. about 0.1–0.45 GB per 16K-row chunk, against 16–128 GiB of logits traffic at 128K–1M keys. ## What this PR does **Kernel** (`csrc/fused_mqa_topk/`). One CTA per SM; each CTA claims 8-row blocks from a global counter (heaviest first) and keeps one continuous Q/KV/TMEM pipeline across blocks: * **Scoring:** the FP8 MQA-logits pipeline adapted from DeepGEMM (TMA loads, UMMA into TMEM, warp-specialized producers). Since relu(s) = (s + |s|) / 2, the weighted sum of the linear halves is a single query (the heads folded with their weights) times the key; it runs on the tensor core as extra UMMA rows, so the math warps only accumulate the |s| terms. * **Sampled gate:** a strided sample of the block's keys gives each row a threshold that keeps a few thousand candidates. The sample histogram is binned relative to each row's maximum over the first sample tile, so rows whose scores share a large common offset still get a tight gate. * **Candidate emission:** keys above the gate are buffered per warp and drained to a per-row candidate slab by two drain warps while the scan continues. * **Selection:** one warp per row selects the top-k from its candidates in shared memory (a sampled bracket, then histogram levels in registers), right after the block's scan, before its slot is reused. * **Exact rescan:** a row whose candidate count leaves `[k, 16384]`, a row with weights unsafe to scale, or a block whose candidates exceed the selection scratch is rescanned exactly in fp32 (the dense scoring pipeline with a streaming top-k merge), so the output never depends on the gate being right. ### Memory * Fused workspace: a pool of 2 eight-row slots per SM, fixed size, independent of rows, keys and context. It is 296 MiB on a 148-SM B300, allocated once per device during the profiling run, so it is accounted against the KV cache: −6,528 tokens (−0.25%) versus dense at the default budget (table above). * The profiling run still reserves the dense logits budget: chunks below the dispatch threshold take the dense path. ### Limitations of this PR -- TODOs Anything outside these bounds takes the existing dense path, unchanged. * **Hardware:** SM100 family only (i.e., B200/GB200, B300/GB300). * **Models:** 32 index heads × 128 dims (e.g., GLM-5.2/5.3, GLM-5.3 kpool, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), top-k 512/1024/2048, FP8 indexer cache. * Not supported yet: DeepSeek-V3.2 (64 index heads), MXFP4 indexer cache, and the DeepSeek-V4.1 two-level candidate selection layers (below). * **Parallelism:** TP, DP (with or without EP) and PCP (with or without DCP) are supported. DCP without PCP is not: each rank holds only a shard of the KV cache, so it keeps the dense path. GLM-5.3-Flash's kpool indexer does not support PCP + DCP itself. Only TP4 is validated end to end. * **Sizes:** up to 1M keys and 16,384 rows per call. The row cap is not a kernel-limitation: larger chunks are not validated end to end yet, so are excluded. Only chunks whose longest row sees ≥ 32K keys (≥ 64K for top-2048) use the kernel. **DeepSeek-V4.1 two-level candidate selection.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 8 indexer layers (`index_source_layer_ids` 2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36). Only layers 2, 8 and 14 use the kernel at this point, which is why its e2e gain is smaller than GLM-5.x (every GLM-5.x indexer layer uses the kernel). See figure below. * **Layer 20 (candidate source)** also writes, per row, the top 2,048 blocks of 8 keys ranked by their max score. The kernel would need a second output and a second selection over block maxima, which rank far deeper than its 512-key gate. * **Layers 24–36 (consumers)** mask their scores to those blocks before the top-512. The kernel would need the block list as an input. * **`indexer_sparse_logits`** (opt-in) already speeds up the consumers by scoring only the candidate blocks, but it requires the MXFP4 indexer cache. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62011 addresses this. ## Performance **Kernel.** B300, real GLM-5.x indexer inputs captured from serving (MRCR 2- and 8-needle and random prompts, layers 0, 9 and 19), one 16,384-row prefill chunk, top-2048, median of `do_bench_cudagraph(rep=200)` over captures. Dense is chunked by the 512 MiB budget exactly as in vLLM and captured in one CUDA graph. | Keys | Captures | Dense (ms) | Fused (ms) | Speedup, median (range) | Fused exact top-k | Dense exact top-k | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 32K | 9 | 2.62 | 2.43 | 1.05× (1.00–1.21) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 64K | 9 | 6.12 | 4.71 | 1.29× (1.22–1.36) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 128K | 9 | 13.0 | 8.76 | 1.49× (1.41–1.53) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 256K | 9 | 27.8 | 16.9 | 1.63× (1.58–1.66) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 448K | 9 | 62.8 | 29.0 | 2.20× (2.11–2.22) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 512K | 6 | 78.4 | 32.8 | 2.40× (2.34–2.42) | 6/6 | 0/6 | | 944K | 3 | 246 | 58.9 | 4.18× (4.13–4.21) | 3/3 | 0/3 | | 1M | 3 | 280 | 62.0 | 4.52× (4.38–4.55) | 3/3 | 0/3 | "Exact top-k": the selected keys' scores equal the fp32 top-k scores. The current dense path rounds its logits to bf16, so it is not exact at the boundary. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61149#issuecomment-6412098207 **End to end.** TP4, B300, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching off. Dense is the upstream base of this PR. Up to 32K every chunk stays dense (below the dispatch threshold of 64K visible keys). At 64K only the last chunk of each prompt reaches it. At 1.04M, TTFT drops by 711 s (55%). The two Flash models gain less in the same concurrency sweep, for different reasons: * **GLM-5.3-Flash: every indexer layer uses the kernel, but each one gains less.** All 45 layers compute the indexer and all take the kernel. Its kpool indexer scores pools of 4 tokens and selects 512 of them, so a 1M-token prompt is 256K keys at top-512 per layer. There the kernel is 1.7× faster than dense, against 4.4× at 1M keys. The kernel's advantage grows with keys, because dense needs more logits windows and each one re-reads every key. The kernel also only starts at 128K tokens (the 32K-key top-512 threshold). * **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: only some indexer layers use the kernel at this point (see detailed explanation above in Limitations/TODOs).** 8 of its 40 layers compute the indexer (the rest reuse one). Only layers 2, 8 and 14 take the kernel, at half-length keys (ratio-2 compressed, 512K keys for 1M tokens) and top-512. **Extending this kernel to other layers is a TODO for follow-up PRs**. * **GLM-5.2/5.3,** by comparison: 21 of 78 layers compute the indexer, all 21 take the kernel, at 1M keys and top-2048. ## Accuracy MRCR shows no accuracy difference: fused and dense agree within noise in every context range. Measured before the latest refactors, which keep the output exact up to ties (real-capture validation below). Context | Samples | Fused | Dense | Difference -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 0–8K | 103 | 0.394 | 0.335 | +0.059 (+0.9σ) 8K–16K | 98 | 0.220 | 0.148 | +0.072 (+1.5σ) 16K–32K | 101 | 0.416 | 0.380 | +0.036 (+0.5σ) 32K–64K | 98 | 0.495 | 0.484 | +0.011 (+0.2σ) 64K–128K | 99 | 0.789 | 0.713 | +0.076 (+1.4σ) 128K–256K | 101 | 0.768 | 0.791 | −0.022 (−0.5σ) 256K–512K | 100 | 0.724 | 0.779 | −0.054 (−1.1σ) 512K–1M | 97 | 0.683 | 0.683 | 0.000 All | 797 | 0.561 ± 0.016 | 0.539 ± 0.016 | +0.022 (+1.0σ) ## Related Work This kernel's sampled gate is inspired by LiteTopK (#48726, arXiv:2607.11976): indexer scores concentrate in a narrow range, so a sampled threshold can discard most keys before the top-k. I open a separate PR because: * **Scope:** LiteTopK fuses only single-request chunks of exactly 8192/8128 rows with 192K–1M keys. Other chunks keep dense chunking, and even a fused chunk needs a separate seed-logits launch and about 2.6 GiB of workspace. Here every eligible chunk (≤ 16384 rows, ≤ 1M keys, multi-request) is one launch with no logits buffer and a 296 MiB workspace. * **Correctness:** on B300 (commit `c7184685`) I found an undersized shared-memory allocation (4100 memcheck errors), racecheck hazards in the candidate ring and the seed/radix-select kernels, and no recovery from candidate-buffer overflow (the mapping kernel traps). LiteTopK's selection is also approximate (99.998% recall); this PR matches dense up to boundary ties. * **Performance:** the only B300 serving data in #48726 shows TTFT within ~1% of stock at ~200K tokens. This PR measures 1.10× at 256K and 2.05× at 1.04M (different setups, so not like-for-like). However, most of this kernel is largely an adaptation of DeepSeek's code. This PR replaces the logits write-out with a sampled gate, candidate emission and in-kernel top-k selection.

commits.pr_title: [ModelRunner V2] Reduce peak memory of chunked prompt logprobs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reduce the peak GPU memory of Model Runner V2's chunked prompt-logprobs computation, which dominates step memory when a request asks for full-vocab prompt logprobs.

## Claims

- `compute_prompt_logprobs_with_chunking` no longer holds every chunk's results twice: chunks are written into outputs preallocated after the first chunk instead of being concatenated at the end.
- Prompt-logprob token ids are returned as int32 (vocab ids fit), taking ids + fp32 scores from 12 to 8 bytes per entry.
- Together: full-vocab prompt logprobs for a 2048-token prompt of a 152k-vocab model (e.g. Qwen2-1.5B) peak at ~2.3 GiB of outputs plus one chunk's working set, instead of ~7 GiB.
- Single-chunk prompts (≤1024 tokens) still return the chunk directly, with no extra copy beyond the int32 cast of the ids.

## Validation

On GB200 (1 GPU):

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k "chunked_prompt_logprobs_match_unchunked or test_all_logprobs or prompt_logprobs_with_chunking_and_preemption or test_prompt_logprobs_mode or test_get_logprobs_and_prompt_logprobs"
14 passed, 7 skipped
```

The new `test_chunked_prompt_logprobs_match_unchunked` (full vocab and top-3) runs 2×1024+3 rows through the chunked path and checks ids, logprobs and ranks against a single unchunked `compute_topk_scores` pass.

## Details

- Motivation: with a measured KV cache sizing warmup (#56492), the warmup's largest prefill with `max_logprobs` equal to the vocab size reserved ~7.5 GiB for this transient on an 18 GB MIG slice, leaving no room for KV cache (`tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_echo.py`, which sets `--max-logprobs 151936`). The breakdown: ~3.5 GiB of accumulated chunk outputs, the same again for the final `torch.cat`, plus one chunk's fp32 logits.
- int32 ids are safe downstream: the tensors are copied to CPU and converted with `.tolist()`; V1's `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu` already uses int32 ids.
- The per-chunk `torch.topk` indices are still int64; they are bounded by the chunk size and cast when copied into the output.
- The CPU worker's copy of this function (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu/logprob.py`) is left unchanged.
- Not addressed: when one prompt is split across scheduler steps, `PromptLogprobsWorker` still keeps each step's results on device until the last step and concatenates them.

## Overview

Populate `usage.prompt_tokens_details` on `/v1/chat/completions/batch` when `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` is enabled, using the existing chat helper.

## Claims

- Sum cached, created-cache and multimodal counts per conversation.
- An unknown cache count leaves its total null; disabling the flag leaves details null.
- Reasoning-token details remain unchanged.

GPU: Colab RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, vLLM `4e3d49dda` with the precompiled wheel built at that commit, torch 2.14.0+cu132, FlashAttention 2.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py -v -rA -p no:cacheprovider --timeout=900
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Skip redundant weight tensor clones for loaders that yield owned tensors
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Drop the redundant weight-tensor clones for loaders whose iterators already yield caller-owned tensors: `runai_safetensors_weights_iterator` with `runai-model-streamer>=0.17.1` (clone kept for older versions), and the pooling-model adapter probe for runai and the other owned-tensor load formats. ## Claims - `--load-format runai_streamer` no longer copies each weight tensor while loading, with `runai-model-streamer>=0.17.1`. - Older streamers keep working: the iterator clones for them, so buffer reuse cannot corrupt weights. - Pooling models no longer clone every weight in the `*ForCausalLM` / `*Model` prefix probe for runai, default safetensors/`pt`/`npcache`, `instanttensor`, `tensorizer`, `sharded_state` and `modelexpress`. - Minimum `runai-model-streamer` is now 0.17.1 in the extras, Docker image and requirements. ## Validation Released vLLM 0.32.0 wheel with this change applied on top (no compile), on CPU and on an H200 pod. ```bash pytest tests/models/test_adapters.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader/test_weight_utils.py ``` | Streamer | Result | Note | |---|---|---| | 0.17.1 | 13 passed (adapters + weight_utils, incl. `test_runai_model_loader`) | no clone, `owned=True` passed | | 0.16.1 | all pass except `..._yields_owned_tensors` | expected: clone fallback is used, test asserts no clone | - Mutation checks: always cloning fails `..._yields_owned_tensors`; dropping the fallback fails `..._streamer_versions`; removing `runai_streamer` from the whitelist fails the new adapter test; whitelisting `fastsafetensors` fails `test_pooling_load_weights_clones_probed_weights` and `test_pooling_prefix_probe_uses_hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
Full runai_streamer_loader/ directory run on Nebius 0.16.1: 40 failed, 25 passed, 1 skipped. 0.17.1: 39 failed, 26 passed, 1 skipped. The 39 shared failures are in `test_runai_model_streamer_loader.py` and come from the test setup, not this change: the 0.32.0 wheel's `runai_streamer_loader.py` has no `runai_pull_files` or `is_unused_weight`, which those tests patch. The only difference between the two versions is `..._yields_owned_tensors`.
Not yet measured: peak CPU memory and load time vs `main` for `--load-format runai_streamer`. ## Details **Root cause.** Before 0.17.1 the streamer can reuse its read buffers, so each tensor had to be cloned to stay valid. From 0.17.1, `stream_files(..., owned=True)` (the default) gives every yielded tensor to the caller and never reuses its memory, so the clone is a redundant copy. **Changes.** - `weight_utils.py`: pass `owned=True` when `stream_files` accepts it and yield tensors directly. Otherwise stream as before and clone. Detection is by the `owned` parameter, not a version string. - `adapters.py`: the probe cloned every weight because the iterator "may reuse the tensor buffer". It now clones only when `load_config.load_format` is not in `_OWNED_TENSOR_LOAD_FORMATS`. - Version bump to `>=0.17.1` in `setup.py`, `docker/`, and `requirements/test/xpu.{in,txt}` so new installs get the fast path - Tests: renamed the runai iterator test (now asserts no clone), added a fake-streamer test with and without `owned`, and an adapter test that whitelisted formats do not clone. **Whitelist.** `auto`, `hf`, `safetensors`, `mistral`, `pt`, `npcache`, `instanttensor` (`copy=True`), `tensorizer` (non-lazy deserializer caches independent tensors), `sharded_state`, `modelexpress` (delegates), `runai_streamer`, `runai_streamer_sharded`. `fastsafetensors` is excluded: 0.5.0 documents independent tensors, but 0.3.3 (the allowed minimum) only clones when `pg.size() == 1`. Custom or new load formats keep the clone until added. **Limitations.** Only the listed iterators were reviewed; model-specific `load_weights` code may still copy. Tests ran on the 0.32.0 wheel plus overlay, not a source build of this branch. ---
